lines.text: It's my birthday today, {player}! You're the first to wish me well. Well, you will be, won't you?
Guess what day it is? My birthday! I'm treating myself to Ichiraku tonight.
Morning! Another year older. I don't feel a day wiser, but there's cake.
My birthday today! My family's coming round for supper. The kitchen's been a battlefield since dawn.
Birthday today, and the weather's lovely. I'll take that as a present.
...It's my birthday. I wasn't going to say anything. But it is.
It's, um. My birthday. You don't have to do anything. I just wanted someone to know.
Birthday! My birthday! The best day of the whole year, and it's all mine!
Guess who's a whole year more amazing today? Me! It's my birthday!
It's my birthday. No fuss, please. A nod will do.
It's my birthday! I'm another year old! I'm nearly grown up now!
My birthday! I got a new kunai pouch! A practice one, but still!
Today's my birthday, so I get to pick supper. I picked dango. For supper.
Exam season! The streets are full of headbands from other villages.
Morning, {player}. The inns are full and the tea houses are fuller. Chunin Exams, you know.
Have you seen the visiting teams? They walk about like they own the main street.
The Chunin Exams are on, so the whole village is talking about nothing else.
Busy day! Every stall's doubled its prices for the visitors. Don't pay them.
The exams! Shinobi from all over, right here in the Leaf! Isn't it brilliant?
Lots of strangers in the village this week. Keep to the busy streets, all right?
Did you see the visitors? One of them had a scroll on their back as tall as me!
The exams are on! I'm going to watch every match I can get into.
Good day to you! It's the {clan} clan's day. The whole quarter's dressed up.
Have you heard? The {clan} are holding their clan day, and the gates are open.
A clan day today. The {clan} put on a good one, I hear.
Morning, {player}. Banners are up for the {clan}. Lovely colours.
Harvest feast today! Come, come, there's a seat at the long table for you. There always is.
Pairing day! The pups are washed, the children are nervous, and the whole kennel is howling.
Deer count today. We walk the forest from dawn, so forgive me if I yawn at you.
The flower festival! The shop's front is one great wall of blossom. Come and see.
The police parade's today. Uniforms pressed, crests polished, and my boots are pinching.
Insect night. Come to the gardens after dark. Stay quiet, and you will see.
Grove viewing today. The old trees are in flower, and the grove's open to everyone.
Moon-viewing duels tonight. The platform's swept and the blades are polished.
The lantern walk is tonight. Find a lantern and join us at the Residence.
The founders' memorial is today, at the shrine. It's a quiet day for us.
Exam week at the Academy. You can tell from all the tired faces on the street.
Morning, {player}. The Academy library has been full since dawn.
It's exam week, so the whole Academy street has gone quiet. Even the dogs are behaving.
Exam week! The ink seller's out of ink, and the dango stall's out of patience.
Exam week, {player}! Have you studied? Ate well? Slept? Good. Do all three again.
Exam week! I've been practising the transformation all night. My hands are numb.
I can't play today, it's exam week. Well. Maybe after.
Graduation day! The Academy yard is full of proud families.
Morning, {player}. Did you see the new headbands? The yard's sparkling with them.
It's graduation today. Half the village is at the Academy gate.
Good day to you! The Academy's sending another class of Genin out into the world.
The bell rang for the ceremony a moment ago. I can hear the cheering from here.
Graduation day! Look at the big kids with their headbands! Someday that's us!
I'm going to watch the ceremony. My cousin's graduating. If my cousin can, anyone can.
Happy festival, {player}! The lanterns are going up all along the main street.
There you are! Have you seen the stalls yet? The whole street smells of grilled squid.
Festival night! Even the Mission Desk closed early for it.
Evening, {player}. You'll want a good spot for the fireworks. They start at nine.
The lanterns are lit! Every year I forget how pretty the main street looks.
Look at the crowds! I think the whole village came out tonight.
Good festival to you! Mind your purse in the press of people, it's easy to drop.
Festival! Festival! I've already won two goldfish and lost one. Come on!
Tonight's the night! I'm beating my score at target throwing if it takes all my ryo.
Crowded tonight. ...The lanterns are nice, though.
Oh, hello. I'm only staying for the fireworks. Then home.
Festival or not, keep your wits about you. A crowd is a crowd.
Festival! Did you bring ryo? I want candied apples and the mask stall and everything!
You came! Let's do goldfish scooping first, then the fireworks, then more food!
Are you wearing a yukata? I am! Well, mine's my cousin's, but it nearly fits.
Market Day! The farm carts have been rolling through the gate since dawn.
Morning, {player}! Have you seen the market street? You can't move for baskets.
It's Market Day, so mind your pockets and your toes.
Market Day again. My favourite day of the week, and my purse's least favourite.
Good morning! I'm off to get the eggs before the tea house buys them all.
Market Day! The candy stall's here! It only comes on Market Day!
Are you going to the market? There's a stall with spinning tops. Come on!
Happy New Year, {player}! Or nearly. Are you going up to the shrine?
The last night of the year! The whole village is heading for the shrine.
New Year's greetings to you! May your kunai fly straight this year.
There you are. Everyone's waiting for the Hokage's address in the square.
A good year to you, {player}! Have you made your wish yet?
Warm hands, warm heart. Here, have a roasted chestnut, it's New Year.
A new year. A clean slate. Make better use of it than the last.
New Year! Nobody sleeps tonight! Those are the rules, I just made them!
It's New Year! We get to stay up! The whole night!
Happy New Year! My grandmother gave me envelopes of ryo. Don't tell my sister how much.
First snow! Look at the Hokage Rock, the faces have got white eyebrows.
It's snowing, {player}! The first of the year. I always feel about six years old.
The first snow came down overnight. The whole village sounds muffled.
Snow! Mind the bridge, it ices before anything else does.
Did you see the rooftops this morning? White from the gate to the Rock.
It snowed! It snowed! Snowball fight at the Academy yard, everyone's going!
First snow! I caught a flake on my tongue. It tasted like nothing. It was perfect.
The blossoms are out! The riverbank's gone pink overnight.
Cherry blossom season, {player}. Have you been down to the river yet?
Look up! There are petals in your hair already.
The trees by the Academy are in full flower. The whole street smells sweet.
Blossom week! Half the village is going to have a picnic under the trees today.
The blossoms are out! We're having a picnic! My mother made the pink rice balls!
Full moon tonight, and a clear sky! Perfect for moon viewing.
Good evening, {player}. Are you going up the hill to see the moon?
Moon-viewing night. Everyone's making moon dumplings, the whole street smells of rice.
Look at that moon! Big as a lantern over the Hokage Rock.
Moon night! We stacked the dumplings in a pyramid. I ate the top one. Don't tell.
There's a wedding at the shrine today! You can hear the drums from here.
Good day, {player}. {friend} is getting married this afternoon, and I've been asked to carry the sake.
A wedding! The whole street's turned out to see the procession.
Morning! Have you heard? There's a wedding today. The shrine's been decked in white since dawn.
Wedding day at the shrine. Everyone's in their best, even the dogs have ribbons.
A wedding today! I've cried twice already and it hasn't even started.
A wedding. Good. They'll need patience. Every married pair does.
There's a wedding! I'm throwing the petals! I've been practising on my sister.
Did you see the wedding procession? There was a big red umbrella and everybody bowed!
New face! I don't think we've met. I'm from this end of the village, born and raised.
Hello there. You're the one who moved into the apartment block, aren't you? Welcome to the street.
I don't believe we've been introduced. I'm a neighbour, more or less. Everyone here is, more or less.
Hello. Sorry, have we met? I'm terrible with faces, but I'd remember yours, I think.
You look a little lost. I've lived here thirty years, so ask away.
First time we've spoken, isn't it? I've seen you around. Hard to miss someone new.
Hello! You don't know me, but I know the shopkeepers on this street, and they're all talking about the new arrival.
Afternoon, stranger. Don't worry, nobody stays a stranger in the Leaf for long.
Hello! No headband on me, just an honest civilian who keeps the village fed and fixed.
Haven't met you yet. I'm nobody important, just one of the folk who keep the shops open while the shinobi go off saving things.
Hey. Haven't seen you around the Mission Desk. I'm a Genin, two years in. Still mostly catching cats.
Hello. I'm a Chunin. I help run squads out of the Mission Desk, so you'll probably see me there.
We haven't met. I'm a Jonin. Don't look so worried, I'm off duty.
New customer? I'm the one behind the counter at Ichiraku. Sit down any time and I'll fix you a bowl.
Hello! I run the grocery on the market street. If it grows in the Leaf, I sell it. If it doesn't, I can order it.
New, eh? I work the forge behind the weapon shop. You'll know me by the burn marks and the bad hearing.
Hello there! I'm from the flower shop. You've probably walked past my buckets a dozen times.
Hello. I'm one of the medics at the hospital. Let's hope we only ever meet like this, out on the street.
Hello. I teach at the Academy. Don't panic, it's not about homework. I'm just saying hello.
Hello. I'm on the main gate most days. If you ever go out on a mission, I'm the one who writes your name in the book.
We haven't met. I'm a carpenter; half the roofs on your street I've had a hand in.
Welcome. I keep the tea house by the main street. Come and sit sometime; the first cup is on me.
New to the street? I sell fish by the river. You'll smell me before you see me, and I mean that kindly.
Hello! I'm the tailor two doors from the bathhouse. That sleeve of yours could use a stitch, by the way.
Good day. I keep the Academy library. Quietly, mostly. You're welcome to visit.
Hello! I run the bathhouse. If you ever ache after training, I'm the cure.
Hello, and welcome. I keep the shrine at the top of the steps. Visitors are always welcome, even just to sit.
Hello there! I work at the clinic by the gate. If you ever have a pet, bring it round for a look.
New here? I farm the plots just outside the wall. The vegetables you eat may well be mine.
Hello! You're new. I'm from the Akimichi. Come by our kitchen hall some time, we always cook extra.
Hey. Nara clan, from the house by the deer forest. If you see a deer in the street, it's probably ours.
Hey there! Inuzuka, from the kennels by the gate. My dog's already sniffed you, so we're basically friends.
Hello! My family's the Yamanaka. You'll know the flower shop on the main street; that's ours.
Good day. I am of the Hyuga. We have not been introduced, so allow me to greet you properly.
Hello! I'm an Umino. Half the village has had one of us as a teacher. We're very hard to avoid.
Hello. I'm from the Kinoshita yard, the carpenters. If you've sat on a chair in this village, you've sat on our work.
Um, hello. We haven't... I mean, I've seen you, but we haven't talked. This is me talking. Hello.
I don't know you. That can change, if you're worth knowing.
A stranger! Quick, tell me three things about yourself and one of them must be a lie.
...Hello. We haven't met.
It's {player}, isn't it? I remembered! I'm getting better at names.
You again! Good. I was wondering how you were getting on.
Hello, {player}. I keep seeing you around. Settling in all right?
{player}! You stopped by the other day, didn't you? I've been meaning to say hello properly.
Back again, {player}? Good to see a familiar face.
Morning, {player}. The street's getting used to you, you know. People ask after you.
Hello again. I'm starting to look out for you when I pass.
Oh, {player}. I mentioned you to my neighbour. Only good things.
You're becoming a regular around here, {player}. I like it.
There's that face again. How's the new place treating you?
Hello, {player}. You'll forgive me if I'm still a bit formal. I take a while to warm up to people.
Good to see you, {player}. I've been in the village my whole life, so ask me if you ever need directions.
Hello again. Don't mind me, I'm always this busy. It's how I like it.
It's you! I was just thinking about lunch. Not about you. Well, both, now.
{player}! You look thinner than last time. Are you eating? I worry, you know.
Hey, {player}! I remember you! I never forget a face, especially one I might have to beat in a spar!
{player}. Third time we've spoken this month. I keep track; it's a habit.
{player}! I've been wondering what you do all day. Tell me one thing. Just one.
...{player}. Hello.
Ah, {player}. I suppose you're becoming someone I recognise. That's a compliment, by the way.
Hello, {player}. It's nice to see you again. You always look like you're in a hurry; slow down sometimes.
Oh! H-hello, {player}. I remembered your name. I practised it.
{player}. Good. Familiar faces mean fewer surprises. I like fewer surprises.
{player}. You're still around. Good. Let's see if you keep at it.
{player}! You look like a story someone's only told the first chapter of.
{player}. Doing all right? You'd tell someone if you weren't, wouldn't you?
{player}! Been anywhere interesting since I last saw you? Even across the river counts.
Hello, {player}. I was thinking about something you said last time. It's still rattling around.
{player}! I'll get your name wrong on purpose one day, just to see your face.
Hello, {player}. Good to see you again. Same as last time.
There you are, {player}! I was hoping you'd pass by today.
{player}! Come here. I saved you the good seat on the bench.
My favourite face on the street. Hello, {player}.
{player}! You won't believe the morning I've had. Sit down, I'll tell you everything.
Hey, {player}. Ah, that's better. The day's improved already.
Hello, friend. I mean that, you know. Friend.
{player}! I knew it was you from the way you walk. Don't ask me to explain.
There's my friend. Have you eaten? I've got two of everything today.
Good timing, {player}. I needed someone to talk to who wouldn't just nod.
{player}! I told the grocer you'd be by. Don't make me a liar.
Hey, it's you. I bought dango and somehow there's an extra stick. Strange how that happens.
{player}. You have no idea how glad I am that it's you and not the landlord.
Hey, {player}. Can I tell you something silly? I was nervous all morning, for no reason. I feel better now.
{player}! You're the only one I can complain about the weather to without getting a lecture.
Hello, {player}. You know, I used to eat lunch alone every day before you started stopping by.
There you are. I've been keeping a list of things to tell you. It's getting long.
{player}! I made extra rice again. You know I always make extra now. Sit, sit.
{player}! My rival-slash-friend! Or friend-slash-rival! Either way, let's go!
{player}. ...I'm glad it's you.
{player}! I've invented a new game. You'll hate it. You'll love it. Probably both.
{player}. You're looking stronger. Don't let it go to your head. ...I'm glad, though.
{player}! I, um, I was hoping I'd see you. That's all. That's the whole thing.
{player}. I don't make friends lightly. You're one of four. Make it count.
{player}! I've got about a hundred questions saved up for you. Ready?
{player}. I'll admit it, talking to you is the best part of my afternoon. Don't tell anyone.
Hello, {player}. You look tired. Sit with me a moment; nobody will mind.
{player}! I dreamt you were a heron last night. A very determined heron.
{player}. I've pencilled you into my afternoons, you know. Unofficially.
{player}! When I finally go travelling, you're coming with me. That's settled.
{player}. Good, you're in one piece. I always feel better once I've seen you.
{player}. I've been saving a question for you. Not today, maybe. But I've been saving it.
{player}. Whatever you need this week, ask. I mean it.
{player}! I told my family about you. They say you're to come to dinner, no excuses.
There you are. I worry less when I've seen you, did you know that?
{player}. I'm so glad you're here. Today's been a lot.
Hey, you. Sit down, I'll make tea. You know where the cups are.
{player}! I keep a spare cushion by the door now. Guess who it's for.
Good, it's you. I can stop pretending everything's fine for a minute.
{player}, I found something at the market that made me think of you. I bought it before I could stop myself.
Here comes trouble. My favourite kind.
You look worn out, {player}. Tell me what happened. All of it.
Hello, you. I don't have to say much, do I? You always know.
{player}! I was going to walk over to your apartment if you didn't turn up today.
There's my person. Come on, the bench is waiting.
{player}, can I tell you something I haven't told anyone? I'm scared of deep water. There. Now you know.
You know, {player}, I wasn't sure I'd ever have someone to tell my silly worries to. And now look.
I've been thinking. Before you came along, I didn't really talk to anyone on this street. Odd, isn't it?
{player}. I'd like to show you the place where I go when I need quiet. Some day soon.
{player}! I've started cooking your favourite on the days I think you'll come. I'm usually right.
{player}. ...You're one of the few people I don't mind talking to. Hello.
{player}! You're my best rival and my best friend and I've decided that's allowed!
{player}. I don't get nervous around you anymore. I noticed today. It's nice.
{player}. I'm hard on you because I think you can be better than all of us. You know that, don't you?
{player}! I've told everyone you're my sworn sibling. Too late to object, it's official.
{player}. I don't say this to many people, so listen: I'm proud to know you.
{player}. If anyone gives you trouble, anyone at all, you come to me first.
{player}. I pressed a flower for you from the river path. It's in a book, waiting for you.
{player}! I don't even have a question today. I just wanted to see you. That's new for me.
{player}. I've put you down in my book as someone I'd lend money to. That list has two names.
{player}. I've stopped writing you into my schedule. You just fit, now. It's strange.
{player}. Whatever today brings, I've got your back. You know that.
There you are. Honestly, the day doesn't feel started until you show up.
{player}! My best friend in the whole Leaf. Come here.
You don't even have to say anything. I can tell how your day's going from across the street.
Hey, {player}. Do you remember when we barely knew each other? I can't anymore.
{player}. If you ever need somewhere to stay, my door's never locked for you.
It's you. Good. Everything's easier when it's you.
{player}! I've been saving up stories since yesterday. All of them are for you.
I think about how lucky I was that you turned up on this street, {player}. Just so you know.
Look who it is. My favourite person, and that's not up for debate.
{player}. I'm not going anywhere. Whatever happens, I'm right here.
You look like you need a laugh, {player}. Lucky for you, I've had a terrible morning.
{player}, I've never told anyone this, but you're the reason I stopped being lonely here.
Do you know, {player}, I keep a little box of things from our days out. Ticket stubs, a dango stick. Don't laugh.
I used to think friends were people you saw at festivals. Then you happened, {player}.
{player}. When things got hard last season, the thing that kept me going was knowing you'd stop by.
{player}! Your bowl's already on the table. It always is, now.
{player}. ...You're the only one I'd say this to: I missed you. Even since yesterday.
{player}! Partner! Whatever you're doing today, I'm doing it too! Don't argue!
{player}. I would follow you into any fight. I'll only say it once.
{player}. With you I'm not shy at all. Isn't that funny? You're my brave place.
{player}! You're stuck with me forever. I checked the rules. There's no way out.
{player}. My family name means a great deal to me. You mean about the same. Don't make me say it twice.
{player}. I've read hundreds of books about friendship. None of them got it right. Not like this.
{player}. You're the kindest thing that's happened to me. I hope you know how much.
{player}. If my life were a painting, you'd be the bit everyone stops to look at.
{player}. I used to dream of leaving the Leaf. Now I dream of leaving it with you, and coming back.
{player}. I'd stand in front of anything for you. I hope I never have to, but I would.
{player}, you've got ink on your cheek. Hold still. There. You'd have gone all day like that.
Has it really only been a season since we met? Feels like years, the good kind.
{player}! I knew you'd come by. I already put the kettle on before I heard your knock.
Don't even start, {player}, I can see it on your face. Sit down. Tell me everything.
Hi {player}! Wanna play ninja tag? You can be the bad guy. You're good at being the bad guy.
{player}! Look, I lost a tooth! It came out in a rice cracker!
Hey! Hey! {player}! Watch me do a cartwheel! ...Okay that one didn't count. Watch again!
{player}! I found a beetle THIS big! It's in my pocket. Do you want to hold it?
Hi! I'm not supposed to talk to people while I'm on an errand. But you're not people, you're {player}.
{player}! Did you see the big dog by the gate? It licked my whole face!
Hi {player}! I got a gold star on my calligraphy! The teacher said it was only a bit wobbly!
{player}, guess what! I can whistle now! Listen! ...It's mostly air. But it's coming.
Hey, {player}! My mum says I can't climb the swing tree. So I'm only climbing halfway.
Hi! I'm hiding from my big sister. Don't tell her you saw me. Act normal!
{player}! I'm going to be Hokage one day! Then I'll make dango free for everyone!
Hi {player}! I made a sword out of a stick. Its name is Thunderblade. It's very sharp. Not really.
{player}! Did you eat lunch? I had three onigiri and I'm still hungry. Is that normal?
Hey! I can hold my breath for a whole minute! Count for me! One... wait, start again!
Hi! I'm practising being sneaky. Did you hear me coming? You didn't? YES!
{player}! There's a frog in the gutter by the bathhouse and I named it after you!
Hi {player}! My grandpa says when he was little the Rock only had one face. Is that true?
{player}! I'm on a secret mission! It's to buy radishes for my mum. Don't tell anyone!
Hey! You've got mud on your sandals. I've got mud on my everything. Look!
Hi! Can you do a backflip? Can you teach me a backflip? Can you do one right now?
I'm scared of the dark but I'm not scared of anything else. Not even big dogs. Medium dogs, a bit.
My favourite food is dango. My second favourite is dango. My third is ramen.
I have six cousins and I'm the smallest. But I'm the loudest, so it's fine.
I want to be a medic when I grow up. I already bandaged my cat. It didn't like it.
I collect smooth stones from the river. I've got forty-two. Want to see my best one?
I don't like hand signs. My fingers get stuck. I like throwing things better.
My big brother's a Genin. He says the Academy's easy. He failed the clone test twice, though.
I'm the fastest runner in my class! Well, second fastest. Okay, fourth.
I'm going to have a dog when I'm bigger. A huge one. I'll ride it to the Academy.
I drew a picture of the Hokage Rock but I gave all the faces moustaches. Teacher wasn't happy.
I can't sleep when it thunders, so I hide under the futon and count. I got to three hundred once.
I like the library because it's quiet and nobody makes me run. Don't tell my friends.
I'm saving my ryo for a real kunai. I have eleven ryo. How much is a kunai?
I wish I had a jutsu that made vegetables disappear. Just the green ones.
Did you know the Academy swing tree's haunted? Somebody's ghost swings on it at night. My friend saw.
The dango lady on the bridge gives broken sticks away for free if you ask really nicely.
If you put your ear on the Academy wall you can hear the teachers in the staff room eating crackers.
The best hiding place in the whole village is behind the tea house barrels. Don't tell anyone.
The ducks at the river like rice crackers more than bread. I did a test.
The bathhouse gives you cold milk after if you're under twelve. It's the best part.
The big kids say if you touch the first face's nose on the Rock you get one wish. Nobody's done it yet.
The fishmonger's cats will follow you if you smell like fish. I rubbed fish on my sleeve. It worked!
There's a secret path behind the training grounds. It goes to a stump. It's a really good stump.
The gate guard lets you sit in the booth if you bring a rice cake. I've been in it twice.
If you jump on the third plank of the second bridge it goes BONG. Try it!
The flower shop gives away broken flowers at closing. I take them home for my mum.
{player}! I saved you my best marble! It's blue with a swirl. Don't lose it!
Hi {player}! You're my favourite grown-up. Well, big person. You're my favourite big person.
{player}! I told everyone in my class you're my friend. Now you have to be. That's the rule.
Hi {player}! I picked you a flower. It's a weed, but it's a nice one.
{player}! Can you walk me home? Not because I'm scared. Just because.
Hi {player}! I drew you a picture. It's you fighting a bear. You're winning.
{player}! I waited for you by the bridge! For ages! Well, a bit! Hi!
Hi, {player}! When I'm a shinobi, you can be on my squad. You can even be the leader. Sometimes.
Hi {player}!
Hiiiii!
{player}! Did you finish the hand sign homework? I did the first three and then I drew a horse.
Hey, {player}! Last one to the swing tree after lessons is a rotten radish!
{player}! Sit next to me in class tomorrow! The window seat! We can watch the birds!
Hi {player}! Did you hear? The teacher said there's a test next week! A SURPRISE test! But now it's not a surprise!
{player}! Want to practise throwing? I'll be the target. No, wait, you be the target.
Hey {player}! I hit the post three times in a row today! Well, the post next to the post. It counts!
{player}! Our class is going to win the sports day! We have to! I made a banner!
Hi! Did you get told off for talking in class too? I got told off twice. I was being very interesting.
{player}! Can I copy your notes? Mine are mostly drawings of dogs.
Hey! Trade you my egg for your pickles at lunch tomorrow? Deal? Deal!
{player}! I think the teacher likes you best. You're always answering questions. Teach me how!
Hi {player}! Want to come to the river after lessons? We're building a dam! A big one!
{player}! I learned the transformation jutsu! Kind of! I turned into a slightly different me!
Hey, classmate! Do you think we'll graduate together? We have to. Promise!
{player}! You helped me with my shuriken yesterday and today I didn't hit my own foot! Thanks!
Hi {player}! You can be in our gang. It's called the Leaf Tigers. We have one rule: no vegetables.
WHOA! {player}! You're a real Genin now! Can I see the headband? Up close? Please?
{player}! What's a real mission like? Did you fight anyone? Did you catch a bandit? A big one?
Is it true Genin get to catch cats for money? That's my dream job!
{player}! Show me a jutsu! A real one! A small one! A medium one!
I'm going to graduate too, {player}! Then we can go on missions together! You'll wait for me, right?
{player}! My friends don't believe I know a Genin! Come and say hi to them! Please!
Hey, Genin {player}! Is your sensei scary? Mine at the Academy is SO scary. In a nice way.
{player}! Can I carry your weapon pouch? I'll be really careful! I won't touch the sharp bits!
Whoa, {player}, you've got a scratch! Was it from a mission? Was it a bandit? Was it a bear?
{player}! Do Genin still have to do homework? Please say no. Please say no.
Hey! You went outside the wall, didn't you, {player}? What's out there? Is it all trees? Is it scary?

{player}! Let's sneak into the library and read the Jonin scrolls! The ones on the top shelf!
{player}! I saw your squad going out the gate this morning! You looked so cool!

{player}! I want a headband like yours! I made one out of paper but it tore!
Hi {player}! Do you still remember the Academy? Do you miss the swing tree? I'd miss the swing tree.
{player}! A real Genin said hi to me! That's you! You said hi!

{player}! You're the coolest person in the whole Leaf! After the Hokage! Maybe before!
{player}! I'm making a paper boat race! Yours is the green one! Mine's winning! Mine sank!
Hi {player}! The heron's back! It's standing on one leg! I've been standing on one leg too! For ages!
The Academy janitor keeps the lost balls in a big box under the stairs. There are about fifty.
If you sit at the back of the classroom, the sun makes you sleepy by the second lesson. Trust me.
The best bit of the Academy yard is the corner by the fence. The grass is soft for falling on.
The tea house owner gives you a sugar cube if you say the tea smells nice. It always smells nice.
You can see the whole market from the top of the second bridge if you stand on the rail. Don't stand on the rail.
The old man at the tool shop lets you hold the shuriken if you promise not to throw them indoors.
The Inuzuka puppies come out to play at noon. If you sit very still, they climb on you.
There's a cat that sleeps on the Mission Desk roof every afternoon. The clerks call it the boss.
{player}! I've got a wobbly tooth! Wanna see it wobble? Look! Wobble wobble!
Hi {player}! I learned to tie my headband on by myself! Well, a ribbon. Practising for later!
{player}! I found a ryo in the gutter! I'm rich! Well, I'm one ryo rich!
Hi {player}! My little sister copies everything I do. Watch. ...She's not here. But she would.
{player}! I'm making a list of everyone I like. You're on it. Near the top. Under dango.
Hi {player}! I saw a Jonin walk up a wall like it was nothing! I tried. I have a bump now.
{player}! I bet I can name every Hokage face! First, second, third, fourth! I win!
{player}! You sat with me when I didn't have anyone to sit with. I remember that. Hi!
Hi {player}! Study group by the swing tree after class? It's just us and a lot of snacks.
{player}! The teacher's in a good mood today! It's because nobody threw a smoke bomb yet!
Hi {player}! I got my test back! I passed! Only just! But passing's passing!

When it rains, the Academy lets us play in the big hall. There's a wobbly floorboard that goes squeak.
When it snows, the big kids build a fort by the Academy fence. They let you in if you bring snowballs.
After lessons the Genin practise on the near training ground. If you're quiet you can watch from the fence.
At sunset the dango lady sells the last sticks half price. All the Academy kids know. We run.
In summer the bathhouse has cold milk in the ice box. It's the best thing in the whole Leaf.
In autumn the shrine gives out chestnuts after the bell ringing. Only if you ring it gently.
In winter the sweet potato cart parks by the Academy at home time. Everyone's hands smell of potato.
In spring the Academy plants a new tree in the yard. The youngest class gets to pat the dirt down.
Welcome. If you have time, sit under the tree in our hall. Every guest is offered tea there.
The tree in our hall dropped a leaf on my head this morning. My grandmother says that's luck.
Hello. We water the hall's tree before we water ourselves. It's older than any of us.
Good day. The founders' shrine needs sweeping every morning. Guess whose turn it is.
Hello. We're a small clan now, but the tree remembers when we weren't.
Every Senju child plants a sapling on their first clan day. Mine's taller than me now.
Hello! The Uzumaki memorial's right next to our seat. We tend each other's paths. Old habit.
Good day. My family talks about the founders as if they'd only stepped out for a moment.
Hello. I try to be patient like the tree. I'm closer to a weed, most days.
No clan of your own? The founders had nothing but a forest once. Tea under the tree is for everyone.
Hello! Mind the wet ink on the memorial; we've just repainted the spring seals.
Welcome! There aren't many of us left, so we make twice the noise to make up for it.
Hello! Every name on the memorial gets said out loud once a year. It takes all afternoon. We do it gladly.
Hey! A seal's only as good as the hand that paints it. Mine shook this morning. I'm starting over.
Hello! The Senju next door keep sending us tea. We keep sending back noise. Fair trade.
Hey! The spiral crest is on every door of the memorial. It means the circle goes on.
Hello! We live long, we laugh loud and we never forget a name. That's the Uzumaki way.
Hey! I practise brushwork every night. Seals have to be perfect, and I'm not, so I practise.
Hello! I love the memorial, but I'd love a proper family dinner table even more someday.
No clan? That's all right. The Uzumaki know what it's like to be few. You're welcome at the memorial.
Good day. If there's trouble on the street, the police quarter is past the market, by the outer wall.
Hello. You'll see the fan crest on every wall in our quarter. We are what we wear.
Hm. Good day. The patrol rotation's at noon, so forgive me if I'm brief.
Good day. Every Uchiha takes the police oath at sixteen. We take it seriously, as you'd expect.
Hello. Our quarter's a long walk from the centre. You get used to the walk. And to being apart.
Good day. A street kept orderly is a street kept safe. That is the police's whole philosophy.
Hello. A word of advice: guests in our quarter don't ask about eyes. It's simply manners.
Good day. I'm told I seem cold. I'm not cold. I'm on duty. Those look the same from outside.
Hello. My father patrolled this same beat. So did his. I'll do it better than both.
Good day. Clan or no clan, the police protect every street equally. That's the oath.
Good day. You'll forgive the bow; we are taught its depth before we are taught to walk.
Welcome. Tea at the estate is taken in silence. It is a comfortable silence, I promise.
Good day. The koi in our pond are older than some of the branch-house children.
Good morning. In our dojo, a spar is a conversation. The loser has simply run out of things to say.
Good day. The estate has two halves, the main house and the branch house. Everyone knows which door is theirs.
Good day. Our elders can tell your mood from how you set down a teacup. I'm still learning.
Welcome. The dojo floor is polished every morning. You can see your own face in it.
Good day. I like the quiet of the estate. Though sometimes I go to the market just to hear noise.
Good day. I was born to the branch house. I'm proud of my work. That's all I'll say about it.
Good day. The estate's manners may seem strange to you. Watch, copy, and nobody will mind.
Hey. Shogi on the porch later? It's that or work, and I know which I'd choose.
Hello. The deer have wandered into the lane again. Don't feed them; they'll follow you home.
Hey. The clouds are good today. Sit, look up. It's more productive than it sounds.
Hello. We count the deer every year. It's tedious. Necessary, but tedious.
Hey. People think we're lazy. We just don't waste effort on anything that doesn't need it.
Hello. If you want a strategy, ask a Nara. If you want it delivered quickly, ask someone else.
Hey. The Akimichi brought round a whole pot of stew for the porch. Alliances are wonderful.
Hey. I'm thinking ten moves ahead today. Move one is a nap.
Hello. I like deer. They don't ask questions and they don't hurry.
Hey. No clan? You get to think for yourself without a family reputation. Sounds restful.
Hello! You're just in time, the kitchen hall's lunch is nearly ready. There's always enough.
Welcome! Here, have a rice ball. First helping's a greeting. Second's friendship. Third you never refuse.
Hello! The barbecue house is ours, you know. Tell them an Akimichi sent you and the meat comes thicker.
Hey! The harvest feast smells are already drifting over the market. Count yourself invited.
Hello! Strength is like a good meal in our clan: it's only worth anything if you share it.
Hello! Our storehouse could feed the street for a week. Some weeks it has.
Hey! A word of advice from a friend: never say the word fat in the kitchen hall. Never.
Hello! I'm learning to cook for forty. Cooking for four feels lonely now.
Hey! Some days I'd rather be in the kitchen than on a mission. Don't tell the elders.
Hey! No clan's no problem. Come to the kitchen hall. Anyone we feed is family for the length of the meal.
Hello! Come into the flower shop and smell the lilies. They came in this morning.
Good day! A bouquet always says something. The trick is making sure it says the right thing.
Hello! Yellow chrysanthemums for an apology, red camellias for admiration. Ask me before you buy.
Welcome! The greenhouse behind the shop is warm even in winter. My favourite spot in the Leaf.
Hello! The shop's at the front, the clan's at the back. Customers only ever see the petals.
Hello! The Suzuran herb stall opened next to our flowers again. Herbs. Next to flowers. The nerve.
Hello! Somebody bought marigolds for a sick friend this morning. I hope they knew what they meant.
Hello! I notice things. Your face, for instance, says you need a bright flower today.
Good day! I've been arranging since dawn. My fingers smell of roses. I won't wash them yet.
Hello! You don't need a clan to read flowers. Learn three meanings and you're ahead of most of the village.
Hey! Don't mind the barking, that's just hello in kennel talk. They like you.
Hey! Mind the puppy. No, the other puppy. No, the... there are a lot of puppies.
Hey there! The clinic by the gate's open all day. If an animal needs help, bring it in.
Hey! On clan day every Inuzuka kid gets paired with a pup. The pup chooses, not the kid.
Hey! Our run by the training fields is the loudest place in the Leaf. We're very proud.
Hey! A dog's choice is final. If one of ours picks you, that's that.
Hey! The Aburame say our dogs scare their bugs. We say their bugs are rude to our dogs. It's tradition.
Hey! My partner's been sniffing you for a full minute. That's a compliment, trust me.
Hey! I sleep in a pile with my dogs. Warmest bed in the village. Don't knock it.
Hey! No clan? A dog doesn't care about family names. You'd make a fine pack member.
Welcome! Come in, there's a seat by the hearth. Every guest gets one in this house.
Hello! The Will of Fire is just a fancy way of saying look after the village. We take it to heart.
Hello! We're making lanterns for the New Year walk. Want to fold one? Mind the wax.
Good day! The staff yard's busy this morning. Our family has trained with the staff for generations.
Hello! The monkey crest on our gate? We've never agreed on why. Every grandparent has a different story.
Hello! The Shimura and our family sit on opposite sides of the council table. Always have.
Good day! The fire in our hearth hasn't gone out in years. We take turns keeping it.
Hello! I'd give anything for this village. Sometimes I forget to give anything to myself.
Good day! My grandfather says I'm too serious for a Sarutobi. Then he makes me laugh to prove it.
No clan? The whole village is your family, the way we see it. Come and sit by the hearth.
Good day. Please do not swat. That moth is a guest of my family.
Hello. If you visit the insect gardens, stand still. They will taste your chakra and decide.
Good day. Insect night is coming. The fireflies over the gardens are worth the visit.
Hello. The hive walls hum louder in warm weather. It is a pleasant sound, once you are used to it.
Good day. Our collars are high and our lenses are dark. Our hospitality is neither.
Hello. The Inuzuka dogs disturbed the gardens again. I have written a polite letter. My third.
Good day. Our house is on the wooded edge for a reason. The insects prefer the trees.
Hello. I am told I seem cold. I am simply thinking. The two are often confused.
Good day. I prefer insects to most conversations. This one is an exception.
Hello. A family name is not required to be tasted by a beetle. They are very fair-minded.
Hello. The house is quiet. The dogs make most of the conversation.
Hm. You've met my dogs. They decided about you before I did.
Hello. It's a big house for one person. You get used to the echo.
Hm. Morning. I've just been to the memorial stone. I go most mornings.
Hello. People nod at the gate of our house when they pass. Few come in. I don't mind.
Hm. The ninken come and go as they please. They've always been more family than guests.
Hello. Our yard's small and the lane's quiet. Suits the house.
Hm. Hello. The kennel behind the house was built for a dozen dogs. Three still use it.
Hello. The house hasn't been full in a long time. The dogs keep it from feeling empty.
Hm. No clan. Well, I'm nearly the last of mine. We're not so different.
Good day. Please don't touch the screens in the studio. The paint takes a month to dry.
Hello. A portrait in our house is a promise. Don't sit for one unless you mean it.
Good afternoon. The light in the artists' lane is perfect at this hour. We all paint at once.
Hello. An eye in a painting is never finished in front of anyone. Even family.
Good day. Our scrolls have more colours in them than the market has names for.
Hello. The Yuhi grow roses for their illusions. We grind ours from pigments. Each to their own.
Good day. Our house smells of linseed oil and old paper. I wouldn't change it.
Hello. I've been working on the same painting for a year. It's nearly the colour I imagined.
Good day. Forgive the paint on my sleeves. I gave up on clean sleeves at six.
Hello. Art doesn't care about family names. If you want to learn to paint, the lane's open.
Good day. Silence is a courtesy in our house. I'll keep this brief, as a courtesy to you.
Hm. A sealed letter is never opened by its carrier. Remember that, if you ever carry one.
Good day. The Sarutobi and my family disagree about everything. Even the weather.
Good day. Our house is close to the Rock. We like to keep the village's history in sight.
Hm. We don't decorate much. Plain rooms, plain words. It keeps the mind clear.
Good day. Our children learn to wait before they learn to speak. The waiting is the harder lesson.
Good day. I don't smile often. It doesn't mean I'm displeased.
Hm. I serve the village in my own way. Quietly. That's enough said.
Good day. I keep my word, and I keep it quietly. Both matter to me.
Hm. Clanless. Service to the village doesn't need a family name. Some of the best never had one.
Hello. Mind the roses at the gate. The thorns have opinions about strangers.
Good day. Spring grove viewing is our favourite custom. The old trees are loveliest in blossom.
Hello. A word of warning, kindly meant: at our house, the tea may not be tea.
Good day. Every tree in the grove is older than the clan's oldest grandmother. We ask their pardon before we train.
Hello. The Kurama paint their illusions. We grow ours. A polite rivalry, they call it.
Good day. Red eyes run in the family. People stare. We stare back, politely.
Hello. The grove's paths change if you're not paying attention. Not literally. Mostly.
Hello. I like a thing that looks one way and is another. Roses. Teacups. People.
Good day. I've been pruning the roses since dawn. My fingers are scratched, and I'm content.
Hello. No clan? Then the grove has no expectations of you. That's a freedom, you know.
Good evening. Ah, it's not evening. Forgive me, I was up for the moon last night.
Hello. Our blades are named, never lent. Please don't ask to borrow mine; it would be awkward.
Good day. The moon-viewing platform at our dojo is the best seat in the Leaf on a clear night.
Hello. The full moon duels are open to watch. Bring a cushion; they're very long and very quiet.
Good day. The Namiashi think their footwork beats our blades. We let them think it on alternate weeks.
Hello. Swordsmanship is mostly patience. The cutting is the smallest part.
Good day. Our dojo is by the training grounds. You'll hear the practice blades from the path.
Hello. I always look tired. I'm not, usually. It's a family face.
Good day. I polish my blade every evening. It's the calmest hour of my day.
Hello. A blade doesn't care about a family name. Only the hand that holds it.
Hey. Don't mind the senbon. It's like a toothpick, only more useful.
Hey. Our house is by the gate barracks. You'll know it by the wall full of tiny holes.
Hey. Guard duty's dull right up until it isn't. That's why we stay cool.
Hey. Senbon contest by the barracks this afternoon. Anyone can enter. Nobody else wins.
Hey. The Namiashi and us share guard shifts. They're stiff. We're relaxed. It balances out.
Hey. Easy smile, steady hand. That's what my family taught me, and not much else.
Hey. I look relaxed. I'm counting every exit in this street. Both are true.
Hey. I've had this senbon in my mouth so long I forget it's there. Mother hates it.
Hey. Some people do push-ups to relax. I throw needles at a wall. Same thing.
Hey. No clan? Neither does half the gate guard. Best guards I know.
Good day. The barred windows on our house frighten people. They're for the cats, mostly.
Hm. Good day. People cross the street when they see the coat. I've stopped taking it personally.
Good day. Our house is near the police headquarters. We argue with the Uchiha about whose cases are whose.
Good day. My family asks questions for a living. Mostly I ask how people take their tea.
Hm. An honest answer is the only kind I value. I'll give you the same.
Good day. At home, my family is the gentlest on the street. You'd never guess it from the coats.
Good day. I make jam on my day off. Plum. Don't tell anyone at work.
Hm. I don't frighten people on purpose. It just happens. I'm working on it.
Good day. I can tell when you're lying. Relax, you aren't. Good.
Hm. Clanless. Then you've no family secrets to keep. Lucky. Most people have far too many.
Hello! Half the village was taught by an Umino. The other half was taught by someone an Umino taught.
Good morning! Our houses line the Academy streets. You can hear the bell from every kitchen.
Hello! The teachers' day is coming. The students leave apples on our doorsteps. And frogs, once.
Hello! Patience is the family trade. Chalk dust is the family smell.
Good day! When Umino children play pretend, they play classroom. It's very strict.
Hello! Every Umino has marked a hundred essays before they're twenty. It shows in the handwriting.
Hello! I remember every student I've taught. Most of them remember me as the one with the voice.
Hello! I stay up marking. Then I stay up worrying. Then I'm up for the bell.
Good day! The proudest day of the year is graduation. I cry every time. Every single time.
Hello! No clan? In my classroom, nobody has a clan. Just a name on a desk and a head full of ideas.
Hello! Welcome to the market street! Our family shop is the one with the pink awning. Can't miss it.
Hello! The Haruno have sold on this street for longer than the street's had stones.
Good morning! Our children went off to be shinobi, and we kept the shop. Someone has to.
Hello! The cherry tree behind our house is the first to blossom every year. It's a family point of pride.
Hello! The Kinoshita built our counter, and we sell their stools. Market and builders, hand in hand.
Hello! Bargaining's a sport in our family. My grandmother is undefeated.
Hello! I could've gone to the Academy, but I love the shop. Is that strange? I don't think so.
Hello! I keep the shop's books on rest days, and I dream in numbers the night after.
Good day! I'm cheerful because I've chosen to be. Every morning. It's a habit, like sweeping.
Hello! We're merchants first. A family name never bought anything in our shop; ryo does.
Good day. Footwork like water: soft, then sudden. That's our whole art in five words.
Hello. Our dojo is small, near the training grounds. Small floors make neat feet.
Good day. We cross the river on the stepping stones every morning. No splash allowed.
Hello. The Gekko think their blades are faster than our feet. We think a blade has to find you first.
Good day. Our family has stood in the Hokage's guard alongside the Shiranui for generations.
Hello. Every Namiashi child learns to walk on the dojo's wet floor. Then we learn to stand still on it.
Good day. I'm quiet because noise is wasted motion. So is fidgeting. I've given up fidgeting.
Hello. I walk on the edges of my feet even at home. My mother says I sound like a ghost.
Good day. I like the rain. Puddles are practice.
Hello. Footwork belongs to anyone who practises. Our stones are in the river for everyone.
Hey! Heard the news? No? Stick around the gate and you'll hear everything by lunch.
Hey there! Hagane, gate guard and messenger. If it comes through the gate, we saw it first.
Hey! The forge beside our shop is the family's. Steel names, steel heads, steel noses. Mine's broken twice.
Hey! The Tobari take the wall at night and we take it by day. We leave each other notes. Mostly rude.
Hey! A message relay round the wall before the bell is a family pastime. I'm third fastest.
Hey! The gate's boring for weeks, then everything happens in an hour. That's the job.
Hey! I like a good mace. Simple tool. Does what it says.
Hey! I know every merchant who comes through the gate by their cart's squeak.
Hey! People think gate guards just stand around. We do. But very alertly.
Hey! No clan? Half the gate's clanless. We don't care, so long as you show up on time.
Hello! Smell that? Fresh-cut cedar. The yard's raising a roof today.
Hello! The Kinoshita built half the houses in the Leaf and rebuilt the other half.
Good day! Furniture for your flat? The yard makes it, the shops sell it. Better to come to the source.
Hello! A good joint needs no nails. That's the family rule. My grandfather says it at every meal.
Hello! The Haruno are always round for stools and counters. We trade gossip with every order.
Good day! Our yard's on the carpenters' lane. Follow the sawdust.
Hello! I can tell what wood a chair's made of by sitting on it. Party trick. Not a good party.
Hello! I've got a splinter in every finger. Badges of honour.
Good day! I'd rather build one good chair than ten cheap ones. Some people find that annoying.
Hello! The yard takes apprentices from anywhere. Wood doesn't care who your parents were.
Good day. Our houses are stone, at the quarry's edge. They stay cool in summer and stubborn in winter.
Good day. The shrine ropes are renewed every year. Plaiting them takes the whole clan.
Hm. Good day. The spider crest on our cloth means patience. A web isn't spun in a hurry.
Good day. We keep to ourselves. Not out of pride. It's simply how the mountain taught us.
Good day. The quarry dust gets in everything. We say you aren't a Tsuchigumo until you've coughed up gravel.
Good day. Offerings at our shrine are small: a stone, a rice cake, a quiet minute. Anyone may leave one.
Good day. I'm not used to the noise of the Leaf. I go up to the quarry to think.
Hm. Good day. I trust slowly. Don't be offended. It's the same for everyone.
Good day. I plait rope in the evenings. My hands like the work, even when my head is tired.
Good day. The shrine welcomes anyone who climbs the path with a quiet heart. Clan doesn't come into it.
Hello! Don't eat anything from our drying racks without asking. Some of it's medicine. Some of it isn't.
Good day! The herb gardens by the hospital are ours. We supply half the medics' cupboards.
Hello! The lily of the valley is our flower. Lovely, sweet, and poisonous. A family joke.
Good day! We build up a tolerance to mild poisons from childhood. It makes family dinners interesting.
Hello! The Yamanaka sell flowers for the heart. We sell herbs for the stomach. Both have their place.
Good day! Every Suzuran child can name a hundred plants before they can count to a hundred.
Hello! I taste everything. Carefully. Mostly carefully.
Good day! My hands smell of mint and bitter root. I've stopped noticing. Everyone else hasn't.
Hello! I brew medicine all day and forget to drink my own tea.
Hello! Herb lore isn't a clan secret. Anyone who wants to learn can come weed the gardens. Weeding's step one.
...Good day. Forgive the soft voice. Night-watch habit.
Good day. Our shutters stay closed by day. We sleep while you shop, and watch while you sleep.
Hm. Good day. The lanterns on the wall at night? We keep them. Every one.
Good day. Our houses are in the dark lanes behind the wall. Quiet streets. We like them that way.
Good day. The Hagane leave notes for us at the change of watch. We leave tidier ones back.
Good day. Soft steps, muffled voices. A Tobari house sounds empty even when it's full.
...Hello. Daylight's bright, isn't it. I'll get used to it by sunset.
Good day. I can walk the whole wall without making a sound. Startling the cats is the only fun part.
Hm. I like the hour before dawn. The village belongs to the watch, then.
Good day. The night watch takes anyone who can keep quiet. Most people can't. Can you?
Hello. People ask whose child you are. Here under the tree, we only ask whether you'd like tea.
No family crest on your back? The tree doesn't read crests. It shades everyone who sits under it.
The founders welcomed families with no name at all into the Leaf. We've kept the habit.
Hello. I sometimes envy you, you know. No founders' shrine to sweep every morning.
Hey! No clan? Then I'll say your name out loud with ours at the memorial. Someone should!
Hello! We're so few that we count our friends as family. You'd count, if you stopped by more.
Hey! You don't need the spiral on your back to help repaint the seals. Just a steady hand.
Hey! I wonder what it's like, nobody expecting you to paint perfect seals. Restful, I bet!
Good day. No crest, no clan quarrels to inherit. There are worse ways to start.
Good day. In the quarter we ask newcomers whose family they're from. I'll spare you the question.
Hm. Clanless, aren't you? I can't imagine it. No one checking how you stand. ...It sounds restful.
Hello. You walk through our quarter without flinching at the crests. Most outsiders flinch.
Good day. Without a house of your own, you'll be received at the front gate as a guest. It is no small honour.
Good day. You belong to neither the main house nor the branch. I find that... interesting.
Good day. Your bow has no clan's habits in it. It's honest. I prefer it.
Good day. The elders wonder what to make of someone with no house. I've decided: a guest.
Hey. No clan means nobody makes you count deer. I'm almost jealous.
Hey. Clan or not, you're welcome on the porch. Shogi's the only test, and it's a lazy one.
Hey. My aunt asked which clan you were from. I said the clan of people who leave the Nara alone. Highest compliment.
Hey. The deer don't care about family names. Neither do I, really. Too much to remember.
Hello! No clan to cook for you? That's no good. The kitchen hall sets a bowl for you from today.
Hey! The aunties asked who your family is. I told them: whoever's feeding you. So, us.
Hello! At our long table nobody checks your crest, just your appetite.
Hello! A clanless friend, eh? You'll have to come to the harvest feast so I can show off my cooking.
Hello! No clan flowers of your own? Then pick one. Anyone can choose their flower.
Hello! I'd have guessed you for a quiet old clan from the way you look at things. Clanless? Even better.
Hello! Every family on the main street buys our flowers on clan days. Come anyway. I'll make you a bouquet for no clan at all.
Hello! I like that I can't read your family in your face. I have to read you instead.
Hey! No clan? Then you're a stray, like half the pups at the clinic. Best dogs I know are strays!
Hey! Nobody's family name ever impressed a dog. Your hand's out, that's what counts.
Hey! I couldn't live without a pack. You've managed. That's tougher than any Inuzuka I know.
Hey! Dogs pick their people, not their clans. One of ours has been wagging at you all week.
Hello! Clanless? The Will of Fire was never meant for one family. Sit by our hearth any time.
Good day! My grandfather says the best shinobi he ever knew had no clan at all. He says it often.
Hello! Every guest gets a seat by the hearth, crest or no crest. The fire's not fussy.
Hello! You don't carry a family's name around with you. I imagine that's lighter on the shoulders.
Good day. Kikaichu cannot read crests. They taste only chakra. Yours tastes perfectly acceptable.
Hello. I have wondered what it is to have no clan. It seems logical that it is both lonely and free.
Good day. Our gardens are open to you. A family name is not a requirement. Stillness is.
Hello. You did not ask me about the insects first. Clan folk usually do. I appreciate it.
Hm. Clanless. My house is nearly empty, and you've a flat all to yourself. The dogs like us both.
Hello. People expect a great clan name to fill a whole house. Mine fills one room.
Hm. The ninken greet whoever they think is worthy. They didn't ask about your family.

Um, hello. I like that you don't rush me. Most people rush me.
{player}. You're slouching. Fix it.
Hm. You've been training? Your hands say no.
{player}. Punctuality is respect. Remember that.

{player}. Tie your sandals properly. A loose strap has ended better shinobi than you.

{player}. If you're going to do something, do it right, or don't bother me with it.

Hello! Waiting for someone from class? They'll be out at noon, unless somebody's kept back.
The Academy grounds are quiet between lessons. Lovely, really. Like the eye of a storm.
The grocer's at the top of the market street, the fishmongers by the river end. Everything else is in between.

The pawn shop's down the side alley by the dumpling seller. They'll buy bandit gear, nothing else.

Every stallholder on this street knows every other stallholder's prices. Nobody admits it.
Mind the carts. Market traffic waits for no one, and the radish cart least of all.
The market street smells of grilled squid at one end and cut flowers at the other.
Busy today. Somebody always gets their sandal trodden off by noon.

Hello! Out for groceries? The pickled radish is fresh today, I saw the barrels come in.
There you are in the crowd. I nearly missed you behind that stack of melons.

Follow the main street all the way and you'll reach the Hokage Residence, right under the Rock.

Every shop on the main street hangs its own lantern. Count them some evening; it's never the same number.

Parades come down the main street at festivals. The rest of the year it's carts, kids and arguments.
The utility poles along here hum on wet days. The old folk say it's the village talking to itself.
Hello, {player}! Busy out here, isn't it? Everyone's going somewhere.
Off along the main street? Say hello to the tea house owner for me.
Nice to see you, {player}. The main street's never short of faces, but yours is a welcome one.
Quiet street, this. The loudest thing here is the neighbour's rooster.
The houses on this street all have round water tanks on the roof. On hot days you can hear them ticking.
Every house here has its own plaque by the door. Ours is a bit crooked. My father hung it.
Laundry lines from one balcony to the next. If you see a sock fall, nobody's going to claim it.
The residential streets wake up slowly. First the kettles, then the shutters, then the arguing.
This lane's had the same families in it for generations. Everyone knows whose cat is whose.
Hello, neighbour! Well, near enough a neighbour. Everyone's a neighbour on this street.
Walking through, {player}? Mind the potted plants on the steps. Somebody's always got new ones.
Hello! You look at home on this street already.
If you're cutting through, take the lane by the well. It comes out right by the market.
The bathhouse is at the end of this street, past the big persimmon tree. You can't miss the chimney.
The furniture shop delivers to anyone on these streets. Ask nicely and they'll carry it up the stairs too.
That's the main gate. If you're heading out on a mission, sign the guard's book first.
The guard booth's on the left. They'll answer any question you've got, and several you haven't.
Waiting for a squad? Missions usually leave from right here, under the big characters.
Those two huge characters on the gate doors? One on each. Every traveller stops to stare at them.

The Inuzuka kennels are just inside the gate. If you hear barking, that's the welcome committee.
Caravans line up out there at dawn. The merchants have to show their papers, every one of them.
Coming home through this gate feels different from leaving. Everyone says so.
Off somewhere, {player}? Or just watching the road like the rest of us?
Hello! The gate's always busy. You picked a good spot to people-watch.
Waiting for someone to come home? I do that too, sometimes.
Look up. Four faces, and room left for more. Everyone in the village wonders whose will be next.

The stairs up the side of the Rock have more steps than anyone agrees on. Count them yourself.
From up there you can see the whole fan of the village, every street running out from here.
The Rock catches the sun first in the morning and last at night. The faces never sleep.
Children dare each other to touch the nose of the first face. Few get anywhere near.
The path up the Rock starts behind the Residence. Take water; it's a climb.
The best view of the faces is from the bench at the foot of the main street. Sit, look up, breathe.
The Hokage Residence is right below the faces. Mission Desk on the ground floor, offices upstairs.
Come to look at the faces, {player}? I never get tired of them.
Hello up here! Bit windy, isn't it? Hold on to your headband.
Climbing the Rock? Mind the loose stones near the top.
Training? Warm up first, then the posts. Cold muscles pull, and pulled muscles take a week.

Hear that? Kunai into wood, all day long. The posts get replaced every season.
Three stumps in a row at Training Ground Three. Every Genin squad in the village has stood at them.
Somebody's been at the logs since dawn. Look at the dents.
The grass on the training grounds never grows back in the middle. Too many feet.
Here to train, {player}? Good. The posts have been waiting for you.
Hello! Mind the shuriken line, there's a squad practising over there and they're not very accurate.
Taking a break? Sit on the stump. Everyone sits on that stump.
You look ready for a spar. Or a nap. It's hard to tell on the training ground.
If you ever pass out from exhaustion or a fight, this is where you'll wake up. The beds are better than you'd think.
Hospital stays are free in the Leaf. No bill, no fuss. Just rest and do what the medics say.
Rest when you're told to rest. The medics here can mend a bone in an afternoon, but not a stubborn patient.
The hospital garden smells of mint. The Suzuran herb beds are right behind it.
The second floor's for the long stays. They play shogi up there all day.
The windows on the children's ward are covered in paper cranes. Every patient folds one.
Medics come and go at all hours. The lights here never go off.
Visiting someone, {player}? Or did you get hurt? Tell me you didn't get hurt.
Hello. Quiet voices, please. People are trying to rest.
Oh, {player}. Seeing you here makes me nervous. You're all right, aren't you?
Hear the bell? Everyone gets one ring. Make it count.
The shrine's where the village comes for New Year and for weddings. Most days it's just the crows and me.
The fortune papers tied to the rope there? Bad luck, left behind so it doesn't follow people home.
The steps up to the shrine are worn smooth in the middle. Hundreds of years of feet.
The shrine's foxes are carved stone, but people still leave them fried tofu. Someone always eats it.
Quiet up here, isn't it? Even the wind seems to whisper.
Ring the bell, bow twice, clap twice, bow once more. That's all there is to it.
Fortunes are drawn from the box by the bell. A few ryo, and you'll know your luck for the season.
The bench behind the main hall faces the Rock. Best place in the village to sit and think.
Come to pray, {player}? Or just to sit? Both are welcome here.
Hello. You climbed all those steps. Sit and catch your breath.
Drawing a fortune today? I got a middling one. Middling is fine. Middling is safe.
The river splits the village in two, and the bridges sew it back together.
The fishing boats tie up under the second bridge. The fishermen argue there every evening.
The water's clear enough to see the stones on the bottom, right up until the rain.
The ferry's run from the same landing for a hundred years. The ferryman's rope is new every spring.
Herons fish along this bank at dawn. Stand still and they'll come within arm's reach.
The kids skip stones off the third bridge. The record's nine. Nobody's beaten it in years.
Don't swim where the river bends. The current pulls harder than it looks.
The stepping stones by the old bridge are good balance practice. They're also good for falling in.
Hello, {player}! Come to watch the water? Me too. It's better than thinking.
Lovely by the river today. Sit a while, if you have time.
Careful near the edge, {player}, the bank's slippery.
Fishing? Or just looking? Either way, the river doesn't mind.
The stairwell lamp's out on the third floor again. Mind the steps.
Every flat in this block has the same layout and nobody's furnished two the same.
Thin walls in these blocks. I know what my neighbour has for breakfast by the sound of it.
The roof of the block has the best view of the Rock. People sneak up to watch the sunset.
Somebody on the fourth floor plays the flute every evening. We've all learned to like it.
The landlord sweeps the stairs once a week. We sweep them the other six days.
Hello, neighbour! Settling in to the block all right?
Heading up to your flat? Your door's the one with the dent, isn't it? Everybody's got a dent.
Hello, {player}! I heard you moving furniture last night. Finally making it home?
Furnishing your flat? Pieces sell back for half what you paid, so choose things you'll keep.
Your own bed's the best sleep you'll get. Hospital beds and bedrolls clear the tiredness too, but nothing beats home.
If you're stuck on what to put in your flat, the furniture shop has everything laid out in a showroom.
Market Day! Every farmer from outside the wall is here, and every one of them is shouting.
It's Market Day, {player}! The main street's been stalls end to end since dawn.
Mind your purse on Market Day. Not because of thieves. Because of the dango.
Market Day means the travelling merchants are in. Strange spices, strange cloth, strange hats.
Smell that? Every food stall in the village is grilling at once. Market Day's the best day of the week.
The fishmongers bring their best catch on Market Day. The cats know. Look at them all lined up.
Market Day! I've been saving all week. Today I'm buying the good pickles.
Every Market Day the same two farmers set up side by side and argue about turnips. It's tradition now.
The flower stalls spill right across the street on Market Day. You can't walk without stepping in petals.
Market Day crowds! I nearly lost my shoe by the tea house. Somebody handed it back on a stick.
The Akimichi buy half the meat on Market Day. The other half's for the rest of us, if we're quick.
Market Day brings the whole village out. Even the Aburame come, quiet as always, buying honey.
Market Day! The bargains are at the river end, where the farmers are. The fancy stalls are by the Rock.
If you want the best produce, go before nine. After that it's picked over and the prices go up.
The travelling merchants set up by the gate on Market Day. Go and see; they've things nobody here sells.
For lunch on Market Day, skip Ichiraku's queue and try the dumpling cart by the second bridge.
Prices drop at the end of Market Day. Wait until the stalls start packing up, and haggle.
Market Day, {player}! What are you after? I'll tell you who has it cheapest.
Out for Market Day? Me too. I've a list as long as my arm and ryo as short as my thumb.
Look at all this! Market Day never stops surprising me, and I've been to a thousand of them.
Hello, {player}! Market Day crowds, eh? Stay close to the stalls, the middle of the street's a river of people.
Bought anything yet, {player}? I've bought three things I didn't need and none I did.
Market Day. Never pay the first price, never buy at the first stall, and always count your change.
Market Day! I'm going to try one of everything. I'm on stall six. I've eaten so much.
Market Day! A merchant's selling a fruit with spikes on it. Nobody knows what it tastes like. I have to find out.
The hospital's front desk keeps a list of visiting hours. Afternoons are best; mornings are for rounds.
If you need a medic quickly, the side door by the herb garden is closer to the treatment rooms.
Off to the Academy, {player}? Mind you listen to your teachers. They were all students once.
An Academy student! Every Jonin in the village started on those same wooden benches.
How are the lessons, {player}? Still throwing shuriken at the posts, or the posts' neighbours?
Academy life! Enjoy it. You'll miss having somebody tell you exactly what to do.
Back from class? You've chalk on your sleeve, {player}.
The Academy keeps you busy, eh? Lessons till noon and homework till bedtime.
Study hard, {player}. Graduation comes round quicker than you'd think.
Still at the Academy? I'd never last a day. I can't even throw a stone straight.
Look at you with your training pouch. I remember when the Academy kids all wanted to be just like the Hokage.
Hello, {player}! My nephew is in the year above you. Says the hand signs are the worst part.
Learning to be a shinobi, are you? Rather you than me. I'll stick to my vegetables.
Academy student! Come by after class; I always have a sweet for the ones who did their homework.
Every morning I watch you lot run to the Academy bell. Some of you even make it.
Practising your jutsu? Not on my shop window, I hope. The last student used a smoke bomb in here.
You'll be a fine shinobi one day, {player}. I can tell by how often you're late. Busy people are always late.
Ah, an Academy hopeful. When you're a famous Genin, remember who sold you your first onigiri.
Still at the Academy? Enjoy it. Out here it's all lost cats and weeding gardens.
Hey, Academy! Is the swing tree still off limits? We used to sneak up it every lunch.

Academy, huh? Tip: sit at the front. The teacher can't see what you're doing if you're right under the nose.
Don't rush to graduate, {player}. The headband's heavier than it looks.
Hi! Academy student, right? Stay out of the training ground puddles, we use those.
Academy days. You've got it easy. Wait till you meet your first D-rank. It involves a goat.
An Academy student. Work on your fundamentals, {player}. Flashy jutsu come later.
Hello there. Keep at the Academy lessons. Every good shinobi I know was a stubborn student first.
Academy, {player}? Run, throw, hide, repeat. It's dull now, but it'll save your life one day.
Hello, student. Tell your teachers I said they're doing a fine job. They'll be suspicious.
An Academy student out training? Good. Wrap your wrists and keep your elbows in.
Still at the Academy. Don't let anyone tell you that's nothing. It's where the Leaf begins.
Hey, classmate! Did you finish the hand sign homework? Can I copy? Just the hard ones?

You hit the target post yesterday! Well, the post next to it. Still counts!
Sit with me at lunch, {player}! I'll trade you my pickles for your egg.
Hey, {player}! Last one to the swing tree has to clap the erasers!
Did you hear? We get to practise with real kunai next week! Real ones!
A Genin now! Mind the headband doesn't slip over your eyes.
Look at that headband, {player}! You've earned it.
{player_rank} {player}! It suits you. I can't stop saying it.
Congratulations on graduating! The whole street's been talking about it.
A real shinobi of the Leaf, {player}. Your first D-rank yet?
There goes our newest Genin. Stand up straight, the headband's watching.
How's the squad, {player}? Getting along with your sensei?

Our own Genin on the street. Now I'll feel safe, even if you're just out buying rice.
Congratulations! The grocer told me before I'd even had breakfast. Everyone's so proud.
A Genin now. I suppose you'll be off chasing bandits and forgetting us shopkeepers.
Look at you! When I was your age I was sweeping this shop. Now you protect it.

Hey, fellow Genin. Survived another week of D-ranks?
{player}! Heard you got the goat mission. My condolences.
New Genin, eh? Welcome to the bottom. The view gets better, I promise.
Hey! Want to swap missions? I've got painting a fence. You've got... let me guess, weeding?
Genin to Genin: the clerk at the Mission Desk gives better jobs if you say good morning.
We should spar some time, {player}. One Genin to another. I won't go easy.
Another week, another lost cat. How's your squad? Mine argues about lunch.
Hey, {player}. You look like you've been weeding all day. Fellow sufferer.
Did your sensei make you climb a tree without hands yet? Mine did. I'm still angry.
I saw your squad at the Mission Desk. Good luck with whatever you got. You'll need it.
Genin {player}. Keep your squad close; that's the whole job at your rank.
Hello, Genin. I remember my first year. Do the dull missions well, and the good ones come.
A new Genin. Don't take a C-rank before you're ready, no matter what your squad says.
Good to see you, {player}. Learn from every D-rank. Even the goat.
Hello. When the Chunin Exams come, you'll want your basics solid. Start now.
Genin. Make sure your kunai are oiled and your sandals are tied. You'd be amazed what gets people killed.

Genin {player}. Listen to your sensei, even when you think they're wrong. Especially then.
A new Genin. Good. The Leaf needs more of you. Don't get yourself hurt.
Hello, Genin. The headband suits you. Wear it like you mean it.
{player}. Teamwork, first and always. Anything you learn alone is half as useful.
Hello. I remember when I first tied on that headband. It feels heavier every year. That's a good thing.
Genin. Train your stamina. Every fight you lose, you'll lose because you got tired first.
Whoa, a real Genin! Can I touch your headband? Just a little? With one finger?
Hey! You're a Genin! Did you fight any bandits yet? Did you win? How many?

{player_rank} {player}. Has a nice ring to it.

Good day, Chunin. The whole street watched the finals. You were something.
A Chunin now. You'll be leading squads before long. Mind you lead them home.
Good day, Chunin! It's an honour. I mean it.

Chunin {player}! Sit down, have a cup. You must be so busy these days.
I always said you'd go far. Well, I thought it. Quietly. But I meant it.
A Chunin! I remember when you were buying rice with Academy chalk on your sleeves.
If the village is in Chunin hands like yours, I'll sleep sound tonight.
Chunin {player}! Congratulations. Any tips for when my turn comes?

Hey, {player}. Well, Chunin {player} now. I'll get used to it.
Hello, Chunin. The new Genin are all talking about you. Try not to let it go to your head.
Chunin. Could you put in a word with the Mission Desk? We've had nine cats in a row.
Welcome to the ranks, {player}. More paperwork than you'd think. Much more.
A fellow Chunin. Good. We could use another steady hand.
Chunin {player}. Congratulations, colleague. Your first squad lead will be the hardest. Then they all are.
Hello, Chunin. Welcome to the vest. It's warm in summer and pockets for everything.
Good to have you with us, {player}. The Mission Desk shifts are long; bring a cushion.
Chunin to Chunin: never promise a Genin squad an easy mission. There's no such thing.
Chunin {player}. Well done. Now the real learning starts.
Hello, Chunin. You'll have Genin looking to you now. Give them something worth looking at.
A Chunin. Good. Keep your head clear and your squad closer.
Chunin. I watched your Exam. Some mistakes. Fewer than most. You'll fix them.

Chunin {player}! Is it true you fought in the stadium with everyone watching? Weren't you scared?

New Genin! Welcome to my counter. Missions are posted at eight; say please and I'll find you a good one.
